title: The document shell
intro_p: By default @render@ emits a bare HTML fragment — ready to pipe into something bigger. Passing @--title@ or @--css@ switches the output to a finished document: the same fragment wrapped in a minimal HTML shell. With no flags the fragment is byte-identical to what oliver rendered alone.
fragment_p: A bare fragment — no shell flags:
fragment_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
title_p: @--title@ wraps the fragment in the shell and sets @<title>@. The text is HTML-escaped for @&@, @<@, @>@ and @"@ — the data is untrusted:
css_p: @--css@ adds a stylesheet link to the shell. Repeatable — links keep flag order — and the href passes through verbatim: URL or relative path, unvalidated. The consumer owns it.
document_p: The whole deal — one command, one finished document:
document_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json --title 'Verdict — dogbed' --css style.css Verdict — dogbed

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
xhtml_p: @--profile xhtml@ swaps the HTML5 shell for XHTML 1.0 Strict: strict doctype, an http-equiv meta instead of @<meta charset>@ (which is invalid XHTML), self-closing @<link … />@ tags, and @xmlns@ on the root element.
xhtml_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json -p xhtml --title 'Verdict' --css style.css Verdict

dogbed 0.1.0 — first verdict

approve — the pipeline sings

Blockers

Nits

  1. ship it
cap_p: @--max-output@ caps the final document — shell included. The k4o stage is bounded by the same value, so a runaway template dies early:
cap_tr:
$ dogbed render share/verdict.knap -d share/verdict.json --title T --css style.css --max-output 250
dogbed: output (297 bytes) exceeds --max-output (250)
gotcha1_p: Dogfood finding: Textile typography eats @--@ in data. A JSON value containing @--title@ renders as @—title@ — the value flows through the Textile intermediate, and Textile converts @--@ to an em-dash. Surprising for CLI flags and technical content; plan around it:
gotcha2_p: Dogfood finding: backticks are not code spans. Markdown habits produce literal backticks — Textile code spans are @…@:
gotcha2_tr:
$ echo '{"t":"try `backticks` for code"}' | dogbed render note.knap -d -

try `backticks` for code
fix_p: The fix: wrap flags in @…@ spans — the code span protects the dashes:
fix_tr:
$ echo '{"t":"wrap flags in @--title@ and Textile leaves them alone"}' | dogbed render note.knap -d -

wrap flags in --title and Textile leaves them alone
